quotes.text:
* MboxMsgInputStream should be regarded as taking ownership of the
 * underlying stream: when the MboxMsgInputStream is closed, the underlying
 * stream is also closed.

/**
   * Start reading the next message, if any. Think of it as a "reopen".
   * The stream must have been completely exhausted to EOF (by calling Read())
   * before Continue() can be called.
   * If no more messages are available (i.e. we've hit the end of the mbox),
   * then `more` will contain false upon return.
   *
   * Continue() will fail if stream has been closed.
   * This is because Close() also closes the underlying stream.
   */
  nsresult Continue(bool& more);

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: A maxAllowedSize of 0 disables the output limit. MboxScanner and ExtractFromMbox intentionally construct unlimited streams because they consume each message and continue to the next. The limit counters are initialized once and Continue does not reset them, so the single-message safeguard should not be casually applied to a whole-store scanner. Close owns and closes the underlying raw stream; Continue requires a fully exhausted open stream. No whole-store scan was run. Static inspection supports this component scope. No runtime test was run for this lesson, and full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion is still pending.
title: Use unlimited mbox streams for whole-store scans and test extraction
